# Actuation, Interrupts, and Virtualization {.unnumbered}

Part III addresses the execution boundary where non-deterministic neural models meet deterministic software environments. We formalize typed tool Application Binary Interfaces (ABIs), confront the architectural breakdown of the $W \oplus X$ protection split in neural models, implement hardware-isolated sandboxes (Firecracker microVMs), red team agent vulnerabilities, and establish transactional consistency across irreversible side-effects.

::: {#pri-vol3-strict-action-abi .callout-principle title="The typed action contract"}

**Invariant**: Stochastic models must interface with deterministic environments through typed, schema-validated, versioned, and idempotent protocol contracts.

**Implication**: Free-form text parsing must be replaced with typed ABIs (Model Context Protocol) and grammar-constrained logit decoding.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-zero-trust-sandboxing .callout-principle title="Zero-trust virtualization and red teaming"}

**Invariant**: Because language models lack hardware separation between instructions and untrusted data ($W \oplus X$ failure), runtimes must assume policy compromise and isolate all tool side-effects inside ephemeral protection domains.

**Implication**: Tool execution must occur inside hardware-isolated microVMs with strict network egress firewalls to prevent data exfiltration.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-reversibility-boundary .callout-principle title="The reversibility boundary and compensating Sagas"}

**Invariant**: Internal state is private, cheap, and reversible; external state is shared, expensive, and often irreversible. Failure recovery requires distributed Sagas with deterministic compensating actions.

**Implication**: Runtimes must stage irreversible actions behind dry-runs, capability leases, and human approval gates treated as $10^6\times$ latency suspension objects.

:::
